extracted.intended_audience: HCI and AI researchers studying computational humor and NLP
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating AI systems that generate humorous meme captions targeted to Gen Z, by instilling cognitive, social, and creative skills and measuring human preference against human and baseline-LLM captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive reasoning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper states that humor is among the complex human skills and explicitly lists cognitive reasoning as necessary. As a production criterion, the model should perform reasoning to create setups, punchlines, and incongruity resolution. (No further operationalization on this page; see full paper for methods.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Social understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is a social binding agent and requires social understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract frames humor as social — effective humor must understand social context and relations. In practice this implies modeling social norms, relationships, and pragmatic inferences so captions resonate socially with the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad base of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor requires a broad base of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors assert that breadth of knowledge is a necessary skill for humor generation, implying the system must draw on wide topical, cultural, and factual knowledge to make relevant references and associative leaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor requires creative thinking; it is an act of creativity that can provoke emotional reactions on a broad range of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creativity is listed as a core skill: systems should generate novel, surprising but coherent associations. The paper contrasts ‘basic LLMs’ with LLMs augmented with humor skills (including creative components) to evaluate the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience understanding / targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience understanding is a required skill; the study targets one audience: Gen Z humor fans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective humor must be tuned to audience preferences and cultural signifiers. The authors explicitly target Gen Z; evaluation and model design should account for audience-specific tastes and norms when judging success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness criterion: provokes emotional reactions / social resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor should provoke emotional reactions and function as social bonding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract frames success not just as 'funniness' but as producing emotional responses and social resonance. Evaluation therefore should assess subjective reactions and social impact (e.g., liking, sharing, perceived relatability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation method: comparative human ratings of meme captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate meme-caption humor by asking people to rate captions from three sources: (1) highly upvoted human captions, (2) basic LLMs, and (3) LLMs captions with humor skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper’s experimental rubric compares the three sources via human ratings (target audience Gen Z). Reported finding: users liked LLM captions with humor skills more than basic LLMs and nearly as much as top-rated human captions. This implies an evaluation metric based on human preference ratings and comparative ranking against human-written benchmarks.
